A court's power to hear cases against all states, whether or not they have consented to jurisdiction
A treaty rule that obliges the Security Council to prosecute every violation of human rights law
A state's power to prosecute certain grave crimes without any territorial or nationality link to the case

questions.prompt: In Arrest Warrant (DRC v Belgium, ICJ, 2002), what did the Court decide?
choices: The DRC had no standing, because its foreign minister was not an official in a position to claim immunity
The case was inadmissible, because war crimes can only be tried by an international tribunal
Belgium violated the immunity of the sitting foreign minister by issuing and circulating the warrant
Belgium acted lawfully, because universal jurisdiction overrides any immunity of an official in office

questions.prompt: A former head of state, now out of office, is arrested abroad for torture ordered while in office, after the date on which the forum state and his own state were both bound by the Convention against Torture. Which authority best supports denying him immunity?
choices: Lovelace v Canada (1981), where the Human Rights Committee held that loss of Indian status breached Article 27 of the ICCPR
Pinochet (No 3), where the Lords held that torture cannot be an official function protected by immunity
Arrest Warrant (ICJ, 2002), where the Court upheld the immunity of a sitting foreign minister from arrest abroad
Roper v Simmons (2005), where the US Supreme Court held that persons who were juveniles at the time cannot be executed

questions.prompt: A national court in State W is genuinely investigating a case of alleged war crimes by one of its own officers. The ICC Prosecutor wants to take the case. What is the likely result under the Rome Statute?
choices: The case is inadmissible under Article 17, because the state is genuinely investigating and is willing and able
The case is admissible, because the Court has primacy over every national court under the Statute
The case is admissible, because Article 27 makes the official capacity of the officer a ground of jurisdiction
The case is inadmissible, because the Court may act only on a Security Council referral of a situation

questions.prompt: Which of these states is correct about the Court's jurisdiction under Article 12 of the Rome Statute?
choices: It may act against any person of any nationality for crimes anywhere, without any condition on jurisdiction
It may act only against nationals of states that have ratified the Statute and the Convention against Torture
It may act only if the Security Council has first adopted a resolution authorising each prosecution
It may act where the crime occurred on a state party's territory or the accused is a state party's national

questions.prompt: What does the 1993 Vienna Declaration say about the universality of human rights?
choices: All human rights are universal, indivisible, interdependent and interrelated, and states must protect them whatever their systems
Human rights are universal only for civil and political matters, while all economic matters depend on the culture of each state
Human rights are universal only for those states that were present at the adoption of the Universal Declaration in 1948
Human rights vary by region, and no regional or cultural particularity may be taken into account when they are applied

questions.prompt: Which argument is typical of a universalist reply to a state that says its culture justifies a restriction on women's rights?
choices: Women's rights are an invention of Western states, so non-Western states should decide them for themselves without any treaty
Cultures are internally diverse and change, so the claim may silence the very persons whose rights are at stake
Culture is legally irrelevant, so no court should ever consider the traditions or practices of any state or community at all
The state is correct, because relativism is the legal rule that is stated in the text of the Universal Declaration of 1948

questions.prompt: A regional court gives a government room to decide how to balance freedom of expression against religious sensitivities because European states disagree on the question, while insisting that torture admits no such room. How is this best analysed?
choices: As a rejection of universality, because the court has held that the Convention is not binding on the state at all in practice
As a derogation under Article 15 of the Convention, because freedom of expression is a non-derogable right in the text
As a margin of appreciation for qualified rights within a universal framework, which does not extend to absolute rights
As pure relativism, since the court has accepted that every right may differ according to each country's own culture and traditions

questions.prompt: A government cites the Cairo Declaration on Human Rights in Islam (1990), which makes rights subject to Shariah, to justify limits on freedom of religion. Which analysis is most accurate?
choices: The Declaration overrides the ICCPR for every state that is a member of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference by its own terms
The Declaration is a binding treaty that amended the ICCPR for all Muslim-majority states by a consensus of its members
The Declaration is part of jus cogens, so that the ICCPR must yield wherever there is any conflict between the two texts
The Declaration is a non-binding regional document, so it cannot displace treaty obligations that the state has accepted

questions.prompt: Which statement best separates questions that the universalism debate should not confuse?
choices: Whether a right exists, how broadly it is defined, and who decides how it applies locally are different questions
Whether a right exists and who decides its local application are the same question under Vienna 1993
Whether a right exists is decided only by each state, and its definition is decided only by regional courts
Whether a right exists depends only on how many states have ratified the treaty that contains it
